input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input only on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`) and never strips a trailing "\r". Windows tools typically emit CRLF line endings, so the last field of the header line becomes "description\r" instead of "description". That fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.includes` check in `assertShape`, which throws `errors.rowShape` for the header itself (index 0 → "row 1") regardless of the actual data — matching the report that every upload now fails and always cites row 1 since finance switched to a new Windows export tool that likely writes CRLF line endings. The fix is to strip a trailing "\r" from each line (or split on /\r?\n/) before parsing.
